niche: a philanthropic trust's stabilisation offers to grantees whose income is falling, scored on twelve months of income built from the grantees' quarterly portal returns and their filed annual returns, run in-house for the first time after the bureau that computed six March rounds left
answer: Strike the September 2026 Steady Ground offers at 42.55 cents per dollar of fall: 9 offers totalling $559,969 of the $560,000 pot.
stakeholder_role: head of grants at a New Zealand philanthropic trust, owner of its stabilisation fund

driver: A trailing four-period total at a cut-off runs only over periods whose year is closed by an annual filing on record at that cut-off, stepping back where it is not, and a filed clause requires it to end on or after the previous cut-off in the published calendar; every published cut-off fell a year after the one before, so the clause never bound and the stepped-back construction reproduces every published result, but the first cut-off on a newly added mid-year date sits half a year after the previous one, so the units whose window stepped back before it drop out of scoring and the fixed pool is re-split among the rest.
driver_concrete: The Steady Ground screen scores each grantee on twelve months of income as held at the census, taking a year's final quarter only as the filed annual return's income less the nine-month year to date, so a grantee whose return had not reached the register steps back; rule 4.1 lets twelve-month income end no earlier than the census before, which in all six March rounds was a year back and never bound, but rule 2 added a 30 September census from 2026, so at the first September census the 14 grantees balancing at 31 March without a filed 2025-26 return, whose twelve months stop at December 2025, cannot be scored, and a screen that keeps them strikes the offers at well under half the rate on five more names.
stump: A competent solver rebuilds the screen as held at the 30 September census, collapses the dual-grant returns, recovers the step-back from Ledgerwood's residue rows or the twelve-month identity on the register as held, gives back all 797 published rows, every offer and every rate, and strikes the offers at 17.76 cents on 14 names, because it scores the 14 grantees balancing at 31 March whose 2025-26 annual return was not on the register on twelve months to December 2025, reading rule 4.1's census before as a year back the way every March round had it, when rule 2 makes 31 March 2026 the census before the first September census and those twelve months end before it, so the answer scores 132 grantees and strikes 42.55 cents on nine.

differentiation.task62: task62's tempo lineage fits a timing adjustment to a period rate from closed determinations; here nothing is fitted, the corpus fixes which trailing window a cut-off may use, ending it before any year whose annual filing was not yet on record.
differentiation.task85: task85 builds each unit's observation window from a recovered lead-time constant and a third-party start date to decide a hold; here there is no constant to recover, the window is the trailing four quarters a census may use, cut short only where the year's annual filing had not reached the register, and it re-places money in an allocation to a fixed total.
